EAMS / Course catalog
Academic year 2026–2027

Course catalog

Thirty-four courses across five levels — introductory natural-history courses for any Brennan undergraduate, methods-heavy major requirements, and graduate seminars open to advanced undergrads with instructor permission.

By level

  • 1000-level — intro
  • 2000-level
  • 3000-level
  • 4000-level
  • 5000+ graduate

Legend

  • F  Fall semester
  • S  Spring semester
  • Su  Summer session

Registration: Most EAMS courses have a soft cap and may be over-subscribed in fall. Students who plan to use a course toward the major should email the instructor for a permission number. myBrennan portal →

1000-level · Introductory courses

Foundational courses open to all undergraduates and counting toward the College of Science breadth requirement. No prerequisites; high-school chemistry recommended for EAMS 1110.

EAMS 1010

Dynamic Earth

4 credits
Offered F, S Prereq none

A field- and lab-based introduction to the rocks, processes, and timescales that shape the solid Earth. Topics include plate tectonics, mineral and rock identification, the geologic time scale, and an introduction to surface processes. Three lectures plus a required Saturday field trip.

Typical instructors: Park (F), Kasprzak / Rivera (S)

EAMS 1020

History of Life and Earth

4 credits
Offered S Prereq none (EAMS 1010 recommended)

A narrative of Earth and life from the Hadean to the Anthropocene, organized around major transitions: the Great Oxidation Event, the Cambrian radiation, the Permian-Triassic extinction, and the rise of mammals. Labs use the Mendel Hall teaching collection of fossils and stratigraphic columns.

Typical instructor: Kowalczyk

EAMS 1110

Weather and Climate

4 credits
Offered F, S Prereq high-school chemistry

How the atmosphere works, from the radiation budget to mesoscale convection. The course covers temperature, humidity, clouds, precipitation, mid-latitude weather systems, and the basic mechanisms of climate change. Weekly weather-map analysis labs.

Typical instructors: Tan (F), Keating (S)

EAMS 1210

The Marine Environment

4 credits
Offered F Prereq none

An introduction to the ocean as a physical, chemical, and biological system. Topics include ocean circulation, marine ecosystems, biogeochemical cycles, and human impacts (fisheries, plastic, climate). Includes a day-trip to the Cobbett Marine Laboratory.

Typical instructors: Volponi (F, odd years), Marchetti (F, even years)

EAMS 1310

Environment & Society

4 credits
Offered F, S Prereq none

A case-based course on the entanglement of environmental science with public policy and social life. Recent cases include the Cape Wind project, Flint water crisis, the New Bedford harbor cleanup, and offshore aquaculture siting in Maine.

Typical instructor: Ben-Ari

EAMS 1410

Natural Hazards: Earthquakes, Volcanoes, Floods

3 credits
Offered S Prereq none

A non-laboratory course on the science of natural hazards, with attention to how scientific uncertainty is communicated to the public. Uses recent events (2024 Noto earthquake, 2023 Maui fires, 2018 Kīlauea eruption) as extended case studies.

Typical instructor: Ito

2000-level · Foundational major courses

Required for most EAMS majors. These courses build the methodological foundation — mineral identification, atmospheric thermodynamics, biological and chemical oceanography — on which 3000- and 4000-level work depends.

EAMS 2110

Mineralogy

4 credits
Offered F Prereq CHEM 1110, EAMS 1010

Systematic mineralogy: crystal chemistry, classification of rock-forming and ore minerals, hand-specimen identification, and X-ray powder diffraction. Two weekly labs in the Mendel Hall teaching collection.

Typical instructors: McAllister, Park

EAMS 2120

Optical Mineralogy & Petrology

4 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 2110

Thin-section petrography of igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks. The course introduces phase equilibria, igneous classification, and basic metamorphic facies analysis. Lab-intensive; students develop a portfolio of annotated thin-section descriptions.

Typical instructor: Ito

EAMS 2210

Coastal Sedimentary Systems

4 credits
Offered S, Su (field session) Prereq EAMS 1010 or EAMS 1210

The processes that build, modify, and destroy modern coastlines: tides, waves, longshore transport, marsh accretion, barrier-island migration, and storm response. Required summer field week at the Cobbett Point shoreline monitoring transect.

Typical instructors: Kasprzak, Two-Hawk (S)

EAMS 2310

Biological Oceanography

4 credits
Offered F Prereq BIOL 1110 and EAMS 1210

An introduction to marine ecosystems, from primary production to higher trophic levels. Topics include the microbial loop, phytoplankton dynamics, zooplankton communities, fisheries ecology, and the response of marine systems to climate change.

Typical instructor: Volponi

EAMS 2320

Chemical Oceanography

4 credits
Offered S Prereq CHEM 1120 and EAMS 1210

The chemistry of seawater: major ions, dissolved gases, the carbonate system, nutrient cycling, and trace metals. Includes a lab component on shipboard analytical methods (Winkler titration, nutrient autoanalyzer, spectrophotometry).

Typical instructors: Okonkwo, Björnsdóttir

EAMS 2330

Physical Oceanography

4 credits
Offered S Prereq MATH 2310, PHYS 1220

An introduction to ocean dynamics: equations of motion, geostrophy, Ekman transport, wind-driven gyres, thermohaline circulation, and a survey of mesoscale and submesoscale processes. Problem-set-intensive.

Typical instructors: Okonkwo-Lin (when in residence), Mahalingam

EAMS 2410

Atmospheric Thermodynamics

4 credits
Offered F Prereq MATH 1320, PHYS 1210

The first half of the BS Atmospheric Sciences theory sequence. Topics include ideal gas behavior of the atmosphere, hydrostatic balance, moist thermodynamics, lapse rates, stability, and an introduction to cloud microphysics.

Typical instructor: Yamada

EAMS 2415

Forecasting Practicum

2 credits
Offered F, S (may be repeated) Prereq EAMS 1110

A daily 1-hour map-discussion practicum modeled on operational forecasting offices. Students take turns issuing a 3-day forecast for the Brennan area and a long-range outlook for New England. Counts twice toward the BS Atmospheric Sciences.

Typical instructor: Keating

EAMS 2420

Atmospheric Dynamics I

4 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 2410, MATH 2310

The equations governing large-scale atmospheric motion: pressure-gradient force, Coriolis, geostrophic and gradient wind balance, vorticity, and an introduction to quasi-geostrophic theory. Sets up the synoptic and dynamical courses that follow.

Typical instructor: Hassan

3000-level · Intermediate major courses

Discipline-specific courses building on the 2000-level foundation. Most are required for one or more concentrations; many serve as the entry point to the advanced 4000-level seminars.

EAMS 3110

Structural Geology

4 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 2120

The geometry and mechanics of rock deformation, from outcrop-scale folds and faults to lithospheric-scale tectonics. Strong field component: three weekend trips through the Appalachians and a required map-and-cross-section project.

Typical instructor: Ndlovu

EAMS 3120

Sedimentology & Stratigraphy

4 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 2120 or EAMS 2210

Sediment transport and deposition, sequence stratigraphy, facies analysis, and basin evolution. Required local field trips to Mesozoic outcrops in Connecticut and to modern depositional environments in Cobbett Bay.

Typical instructor: Kasprzak

EAMS 3130

Geomorphology

4 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 1010

The processes that shape the Earth's surface: weathering, hillslope evolution, fluvial systems, glacial geomorphology, and chemical denudation. Lab work uses LiDAR-derived topography from the Brennan Geological Reserve.

Typical instructor: Rivera

EAMS 3210

Igneous & Metamorphic Petrology

4 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 2120

Advanced petrology of igneous and metamorphic rocks. Topics include phase diagrams, geothermobarometry, isotope tracers for magma sources, and a survey of major tectonic settings (mid-ocean ridge, arc, continental rift, orogenic belt).

Typical instructor: Ito

EAMS 3220

Sea-going Methods

4 credits
Offered F Prereq any 2300-level course; instructor permission

A hands-on course in shipboard oceanographic methods: CTD operation, water sampling, sediment coring, and shipboard analytical chemistry. Includes a required 5-day cruise on the R/V Cobbett Bay during fall break.

Typical instructors: Greene, rotating area faculty

EAMS 3230

Marine Geochemistry

3 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 2320

Quantitative marine geochemistry: residence times, isotopic tracers, sediment-water exchange, and the marine carbon cycle. Includes a 3-week independent project on a published data set from the GEOTRACES program.

Typical instructors: Okonkwo, Björnsdóttir

EAMS 3310

Climate Change Science & Policy

4 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 1110 or EAMS 1010

The scientific basis for anthropogenic climate change, paired with the policy mechanisms (Paris Agreement, US Clean Air Act, state-level RGGI) that respond to it. Co-taught with the Department of Public Policy.

Typical instructors: Tan, Ben-Ari, plus PUBP faculty

EAMS 3410

Atmospheric Dynamics II

4 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 2420

Quasi-geostrophic theory, baroclinic instability, Rossby wave dynamics, and the general circulation of the atmosphere. The course pairs analytical problem sets with computational exercises in Python.

Typical instructor: Hassan

EAMS 3420

Synoptic Meteorology

4 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 2420

Mid-latitude weather systems: extratropical cyclones, frontal structure, jet streaks, blocking, and severe weather. Case studies use the Brennan reanalysis composite catalog.

Typical instructor: Tan

EAMS 3430

Atmospheric Chemistry

3 credits
Offered S Prereq CHEM 1120, EAMS 1110

Photochemistry of the troposphere and stratosphere: OH chemistry, NOx and VOCs, ozone, the sulfur cycle, and an introduction to secondary organic aerosol formation. Lab demonstrations in the Adeyemi group's mass-spectrometry suite.

Typical instructors: Adeyemi, Jensen

EAMS 3510

Introduction to GIS for Earth Scientists

3 credits
Offered F, S Prereq any 1000-level EAMS course

A practical introduction to geographic information systems for earth scientists. Topics include vector and raster data, projections, basic spatial analysis, and the production of publication-quality maps. Software: QGIS and ArcGIS Pro.

Typical instructor: Mendoza

4000-level · Advanced undergraduate courses

Topical advanced courses, mostly taken by juniors and seniors in the major. Most have small enrollment and a substantial independent project. The capstone courses (EAMS 4910 and EAMS 4990) also live at this level.

EAMS 4110

Tectonics

3 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 3110

A regional and theoretical course on the assembly and evolution of continents, with case studies from the Appalachians, the European Alps, and the Tibetan plateau. Emphasizes the integration of structural, geochronologic, and geodynamic evidence.

Typical instructors: Ndlovu, Petrov (alternating years)

EAMS 4220

Submarine Geology

3 credits
Offered S (alternating years) Prereq EAMS 3120 or EAMS 3220

The geology of the seafloor: mid-ocean ridge systems, deep-sea sedimentation, continental slope instability, and gas hydrates. Includes a multi-week project using multibeam bathymetry from the Gulf of Maine.

Typical instructors: Bhatt, Thurston (when offered)

EAMS 4310

Marine Ecology

3 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 2310

Population and community ecology in marine systems: rocky intertidal communities, kelp forests, fisheries, marine heatwaves, and the ecology of cold-temperate vs. tropical reefs. Weekly readings from the primary literature.

Typical instructor: Volponi

EAMS 4320

Estuarine Biogeochemistry

3 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 2320

The coupled physical, chemical, and biological processes that drive nutrient and trace-metal cycling in estuaries. Major case study each year: Cobbett Bay, Long Island Sound, or Chesapeake Bay (rotating).

Typical instructor: Okonkwo

EAMS 4410

Climate Dynamics

3 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 3410 or instructor permission

The dynamics of the climate system: ocean-atmosphere coupling, ENSO, the monsoon, modes of mid-latitude variability, and an introduction to paleoclimate modeling. Strong python/numpy component.

Typical instructors: Yamada, Tan

EAMS 4420

Boundary-Layer Meteorology

3 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 2420

The physics of the lowest 1–2 km of the atmosphere, where most of human exposure to weather occurs. Topics include surface energy balance, turbulence closure, the diurnal cycle, and the marine boundary layer.

Typical instructor: Adeyemi

EAMS 4510

Paleoclimate

3 credits
Offered F Prereq EAMS 1110 or EAMS 1020

Methods and results in paleoclimate reconstruction: ice cores, tree rings, marine sediment isotope records, lake varves, and corals. Students complete a quantitative reconstruction project on a published dataset.

Typical instructor: Rasmussen

EAMS 4910

Summer Field Camp

6 credits
Offered Su (4 weeks) Prereq EAMS 3110, EAMS 3120

The capstone field course for the BA in Earth Sciences. Four weeks based at the Brennan Geological Reserve in central Maine, with students working in pairs to produce a 1:24,000 geologic map and structural interpretation of an assigned quadrangle. Limited enrollment.

Typical instructors: FitzGerald (lead), rotating EAMS faculty

EAMS 4990

Senior Research Thesis

3 cr. / semester (6 total)
Offered F & S (two-semester sequence) Prereq faculty thesis advisor; senior standing

An independent two-semester research project, supervised by a faculty advisor and concluding with a public defense in late April. Required for the BS Atmospheric, BS Marine, and joint BA Environmental Studies degrees; optional for the BA Earth Sciences in place of field camp.

Instructor: faculty thesis advisor

5000+ · Graduate courses

Graduate courses, ordinarily taken by master's and PhD students. Advanced undergraduates with the necessary prerequisites may enroll with the instructor's written permission; this is common for 5500-level data-science courses.

EAMS 5210

Advanced Marine Geochemistry

3 credits
Offered F Prereq graduate standing; EAMS 3230 or equiv.

A research-oriented graduate seminar on current problems in marine geochemistry. Each year focuses on a single theme — recent themes have included reactive iron cycling, anthropogenic carbon storage, and oxygen-minimum-zone biogeochemistry.

Typical instructors: Okonkwo, Singh, Björnsdóttir (rotating)

EAMS 5220

Coastal Adaptation Science & Policy

3 credits
Offered S Prereq graduate standing

A multi-disciplinary graduate seminar on the science and governance of coastal adaptation. Combines physical-science readings (sea-level rise, marsh dynamics, storm surge) with case studies of municipal adaptation planning in Massachusetts, North Carolina, and Louisiana.

Typical instructors: Arroyo, Ben-Ari

EAMS 5310

Climate Dynamics (graduate)

3 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 3410 or equivalent

A graduate-level treatment of climate dynamics: the general circulation, modes of internal variability, anthropogenic forcing and the role of feedbacks, and an introduction to the analysis of CMIP-style multi-model ensembles.

Typical instructor: Yamada

EAMS 5410

Data Assimilation

3 credits
Offered F Prereq linear algebra; graduate standing

Methods for combining observations with dynamical models, from optimal interpolation through 3D-Var, 4D-Var, and ensemble Kalman filters. Required for the Pro MS in Environmental Data Science.

Typical instructors: Novak, Yamada

EAMS 5510

Reproducible Geoscience Computing

3 credits
Offered F Prereq graduate standing or instructor permission

A required first-year graduate methods course: version control, project organization, environments and dependency management, basic shell scripting, and the production of reproducible figures from raw data. Software-agnostic; examples in both Python and R.

Typical instructor: Mendoza

EAMS 5520

Geospatial Analysis with R & Python

3 credits
Offered S Prereq EAMS 5510 or equivalent

Computational geospatial analysis for environmental data scientists: raster and vector processing at scale, spatial statistics, remote-sensing workflows, and the production of publication-quality maps. Project: an end-to-end analysis on a student-chosen dataset.

Typical instructor: Mendoza

EAMS 5530

Machine Learning for Earth Science

3 credits
Offered F Prereq linear algebra; programming in Python

Supervised and unsupervised machine learning applied to geoscience problems, with emphasis on the pitfalls specific to earth-science data: spatial autocorrelation, distribution shift, and physical-consistency constraints. Final group project benchmarks methods on a published dataset.

Typical instructor: Novak

EAMS 5980

Applied Capstone (Pro MS)

6 credits
Offered Su Prereq enrollment in the Pro MS

The summer capstone for the Professional MS in Environmental Data Science. Students work in pairs with an external partner (a state agency, NGO, or consulting firm) to deliver a defined analytical product, with a faculty co-supervisor.

Instructors: Novak (coordinator), partner co-supervisors

EAMS 5990

Thesis Research

variable, 1–6 cr.
Offered F, S, Su Prereq graduate standing; thesis advisor

Faculty-supervised thesis research credit for master's and pre-candidacy PhD students. Variable credit; students typically enroll for 3–6 credits per semester during the thesis-writing phase.

Instructor: thesis advisor
